# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT → probe gap: live-tile entries are not bootability-checked**

`missingEntry` probes only `AppStorage.entryPath(id)` (`apps/<id>/widget.js`) — the full-app boot entry. An app with a manifest `"widget"` section boots its tile through `tileWidget.entry` (e.g. `widget_tile.js`, see `JsAppInfo.tileWidgetPath`), and that file is **not** probed. A stored tile app whose `widget.js` exists but whose tile entry was lost (the exact torn-snapshot shape this PR fixes) lists **clean** and the tile boot still dies with a `StateError` — honest now, but not the missing-files state I2 promises.

```dart
final missingEntry = ((await _env.exists(AppStorage.entryPath(id))).valueOrNull ?? false)

```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: install-side i18n-ref rejection is inconsistent with the read side — and stricter than before**

`_withI18nContents` (read side) handles a non-conforming ref by skipping it like a missing file (log + fall through to the next locale). Here (install side) `AppStorage.appFile(id, ref)` **throws** for the same shapes, so an update archive omitting a ref file whose name carries a space or a non-ASCII char fails install with the raw `path "…" cannot be resolved under apps/<id>/` message instead of the designed `i18n ref "…" is missing` StateError. Note `normalizeRefPath` (manifest_i18n.dart:169) accepts such names while `_segmentPattern` (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`) rejects them — refs that installed fine before this PR can now fail.

Two cheap alignments:

```dart
for (final ref in refs) {

  if (!AppStorage.isValidRelativePath(ref)) {

  }
  ...
}
```

Also: `installWidget`'s new hostile-entry-name rejection (an `ArgumentError` per archive file) has no direct test — `test/apps/app_storage_test.dart` covers the resolver but no test drives `installWidget(files: {'../evil.js': …})` to an install failure.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: third manual 14-field copy — extract a `copyWith`**

`withError` duplicates the full field-by-field copy already written out in `withI18nContents` (and mirrored by the primary constructor's 15 params). The next `JsAppInfo` field must now be threaded through three hand-maintained copies — the classic drift hazard (a missed field silently drops state on flag).

```dart

  declaredPermissions: declaredPermissions, nameText: nameText,
  descriptionText: descriptionText, version: version, chrome: chrome,

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT → probe gap: live-tile entries are not bootability-checked**

`missingEntry` probes only `AppStorage.entryPath(id)` (`apps/<id>/widget.js`) — the full-app boot entry. ## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT → probe gap: live-tile entries are not bootability-checked**

`missingEntry` probes only `AppStorage.entryPath(id)` (`apps/<id>/widget.js`) — the full-app boot entry. An app with a manifest `"widget"` section boots its tile through `tileWidget.entry` (e.g. `widget_tile.js`, see `JsAppInfo.tileWidgetPath`), and that file is **not** probed. A stored tile app whose `widget.js` exists but whose tile entry was lost (the exact torn-snapshot shape this PR fixes) lists **clean** and the tile boot still dies with a `StateError` — honest now, but not the missing-files state I2 promises.

Suggestion: when `tileWidget != null`, also probe `tileWidgetPath` (extend `_missingEntryMessage` with the tile path) so every listed launch surface carries the explicit state.

```dart
final missingEntry = ((await _env.exists(AppStorage.entryPath(id))).valueOrNull ?? false)
    ? null
    : _missingEntryMessage(id);
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: install-side i18n-ref rejection is inconsistent with the read side — and stricter than before**

`_withI18nContents` (read side) handles a non-conforming ref by skipping it like a missing file (log + fall through to the next locale). Here (install side) `AppStorage.appFile(id, ref)` **throws** for the same shapes, so an update archive omitting a ref file whose name carries a space or a non-ASCII char fails install with the raw `path "…" cannot be resolved under apps/<id>/` message instead of the designed `i18n ref "…" is missing` StateError. Note `normalizeRefPath` (manifest_i18n.dart:169) accepts such names while `_segmentPattern` (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`) rejects them — refs that installed fine before this PR can now fail.

Two cheap alignments:

```dart
for (final ref in refs) {
  if (files.containsKey(ref)) continue;
  if (!AppStorage.isValidRelativePath(ref)) {
    throw StateError('install of $id rejected: manifest i18n ref "$ref" is not a '
        'valid in-namespace path'); // honest, consistent with the read side
  }
  ...
}
```

(or widen `_segmentPattern` if unicode/space asset names are meant to stay installable). Also: `installWidget`'s new hostile-entry-name rejection (an `ArgumentError` per archive file) has no direct test — `test/apps/app_storage_test.dart` covers the resolver but no test drives `installWidget(files: {'../evil.js': …})` to an install failure.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: third manual 14-field copy — extract a `copyWith`**

`withError` duplicates the full field-by-field copy already written out in `withI18nContents` (and mirrored by the primary constructor's 15 params). The next `JsAppInfo` field must now be threaded through three hand-maintained copies — the classic drift hazard (a missed field silently drops state on flag).

```dart
JsAppInfo copyWith({String? error}) => JsAppInfo(
  id: id, name: name, description: description, icon: icon,
  declaredPermissions: declaredPermissions, nameText: nameText,
  descriptionText: descriptionText, version: version, chrome: chrome,
  tileWidget: tileWidget, bundled: bundled, platforms: platforms,
  dirOverride: dirOverride, error: error ?? this.error,
);
```

then `withI18nContents`/`withError` (and future flag setters) become one-liners over it.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `Party-Time` is not a hostile name under this PR's own design — the fixture tests the wrong gate**

`isResolvableId('Party-Time')` is **true** by design (the escape floor deliberately keeps legacy ids the strict `idPattern` rejects — that's the two-layer story in `AppStorage`'s doc comment). So this entry is excluded here only because the fixture never writes it a `manifest.json`, not because the list-side id gate rejected it. As written, the assertion `apps.map((a) => a.id), ['ok']` passes for a reason the test name doesn't claim, and the legacy-floor half of the AC4 story stays unpinned at the integration level (it is covered only by the pure `AppStorage` UT).

# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1619
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1619
- **Title**: gh-1614 [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1614` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +1239
- **Deletions**: -35
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:14:41Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T06:01:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1614
### What changed

- One app-storage namespace (gh-1614 I1): new `AppStorage` resolver (`flutter_app/lib/apps/app_storage.dart`) is the single place resolving `apps/<id>/…` for listing (`AppsStore.listApps`), booting (`JsAppEngine`'s widget reader) and catalog installs (`installWidget`) — one validator, one clamp, no second path normalization.
- Listed ⇒ bootable (I2): `listApps` probes the boot entry through the same resolver; a listed app whose stored files are missing now renders the explicit "stored files missing" state naming the root and the exact path, instead of a tile that dies with `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` on tap.
- Honest failures (I3): entry-assembly failures name the storage root and every missing file; the widget-file reader clamps assembler paths (`jsr.include`, manifest `files`, imports) under the app dir, and traversal/absolute ids are rejected at list and read (AC4).

### Key decisions

- Shared pure resolver over a stateful facade (ticket open question 2): path math only, so VM/web/extension resolve identically.
- Two validation layers: strict `idPattern` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, the canonical new-id rule) plus an escape floor (`isResolvableId`) for ids already in user storage — legacy dirs like `bad_types` keep listing, while `../x`/absolute/separator ids never resolve.
- The manifest-declared `id` no longer overrides the storage dir name — a divergent declared id was itself a listed-unreadable vector (tile resolving a different root than storage).
- Reuses the #866 broken-app machinery (`JsAppInfo.error` badge + copyable dialog on every launch surface) — no new UI.

### How to verify

```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/app_storage_test.dart test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart test/apps/apps_store_test.dart test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart
```

- AC1/AC3/AC4 + the root-resolution REG live in `test/apps/app_namespace_it_test.dart` (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`, torn-snapshot restore, hostile listings).
- Extension e2e (AC2) is not runnable in this environment (needs `scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` + Chrome); the Dart-side IT pins the same listing + entry-assembly path the panel build executes — the `browser_ext/e2e` harness picks up the install-then-open journey when a bundled build exists.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[AppsStore.listApps] --> R[AppStorage resolver]
  B[JsAppEngine boot reader] --> R
  I[installWidget writes] --> R
  R -->|valid id, clamped path| E[ExecutionEnv apps/<id>/…]
  R -->|traversal / absolute| X[rejected before any IO]
  L -->|entry missing| S[stored-files-missing state]
  B -->|entry missing| H[honest failure: root + missing paths]
```

</details>
