💡 **SUGGESTION: install-side i18n-ref rejection is inconsistent with the read side — and stricter than before**

`_withI18nContents` (read side) handles a non-conforming ref by skipping it like a missing file (log + fall through to the next locale). Here (install side) `AppStorage.appFile(id, ref)` **throws** for the same shapes, so an update archive omitting a ref file whose name carries a space or a non-ASCII char fails install with the raw `path "…" cannot be resolved under apps/<id>/` message instead of the designed `i18n ref "…" is missing` StateError. Two cheap alignments:

```dart
for (final ref in refs) {
  if (files.containsKey(ref)) continue;
  if (!AppStorage.isValidRelativePath(ref)) {
    throw StateError('install of $id rejected: manifest i18n ref "$ref" is not a '
        'valid in-namespace path'); // honest, consistent with the read side
  }
  ...
}
```

Also: `installWidget`'s new hostile-entry-name rejection (an `ArgumentError` per archive file) has no direct test — `test/apps/app_storage_test.dart` covers the resolver but no test drives `installWidget(files: {'../evil.js': …})` to an install failure.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: third manual 14-field copy — extract a `copyWith`**

`withError` duplicates the full field-by-field copy already written out in `withI18nContents` (and mirrored by the primary constructor's 15 params). The next `JsAppInfo` field must now be threaded through three hand-maintained copies — the classic drift hazard (a missed field silently drops state on flag).

```dart
JsAppInfo copyWith({String? error}) => JsAppInfo(

  descriptionText: descriptionText, version: version, chrome: chrome,

  dirOverride: dirOverride, error: error ?? this.error,

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `Party-Time` is not a hostile name under this PR's own design — the fixture tests the wrong gate**

`isResolvableId('Party-Time')` is **true** by design (the escape floor deliberately keeps legacy ids the strict `idPattern` rejects — that's the two-layer story in `AppStorage`'s doc comment). # gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.
</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.

blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. blocks.text:
# gh-1614: [GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')

## Description

## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

---

Chrome extension: opening "2048 Мини 🎲" fails — `Bad state: app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js` (thrown from `JsAppEngine` when manifest/entry unreadable via the ExecutionEnv). Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

{
  "key": "gh-1614",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Extension app storage: list and read share one namespace — stored JS apps always start (kills 'app entry not found')",
    "description": "## Goal — one app-storage namespace (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **every JS app the extension's Apps tab can list is an app it can start** — listing and reading go through one resolved storage root, so "app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js" becomes impossible for any listed app.

Today in the Chrome extension (side panel = Flutter web build) an app can appear in the Apps list while its entry files cannot be read: `JsAppEngine` throws `StateError('app entry not found: apps/2048/widget.js')` when `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` or `effective.readJs` returns null through the web `ExecutionEnv` (OPFS/`fs_store.js` backed). Listed-but-unreadable ⇒ listing and reading resolve different roots/namespaces (or the entry was never persisted). Bundled `subscription-tracker` works; user-created apps break.

## Why this framing
- The defect is a **namespace divergence**, not a missing file: the fix is one resolved root for list/read/write on web, plus honest failure naming. Retracted framing: "bundle all apps into the extension" — user-created apps are storage-resident by design.

## Architecture
- Components: `_AppWidgetFileReader` (ExecutionEnv reader), `WidgetManifest.fromStorage`, `JsAppEngine` boot/entry-assembly, the web env's project-mount root (OPFS).
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (single root):** Apps-tab listing and app reads resolve `apps/<id>/` against the same mount root on every host (VM / web / extension). Asserted by a shared resolution helper — no second path normalization.
  - **I2 (list ⇒ startable):** anything listed in the Apps tab passes a bootability check (manifest + entry readable) or renders an explicit "stored files missing" state with the root that was searched — never a raw `StateError`.
  - **I3 (honest failure):** the error names the storage root and the exact missing paths.

## Capability surface
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List apps | one root | same root as read (I1) |
| Start app | `StateError` on miss | bootability check + actionable state (I2/I3) |
| Bundled apps | work | unchanged, REG-guarded |
| User-created apps | broken on extension | first-class (IT via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e) |
| Cross-host created app appearing in extension list | divergent listing | either present-and-startable or absent — never listed-unreadable |
| Diagnostics | none | app storage inspector note (root path + per-app file presence) — second tier |

## Security (web storage namespace)
- Threat: app ids/paths arriving from user storage must not escape the `apps/` namespace (path traversal `../`, absolute ids, unicode normalization duplicates). I1's shared helper validates id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` and clamps resolution under the mount root — impossible-by-construction escapes, byte-scan test for `..`/absolute segments.
- Apps remain pure `jsr.render` widgets: no fs/network beyond manifest-declared fetches (unchanged; #1616 covers the load path).

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — IT (web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`): app in `apps/<id>/` boots through the same entry-assembly path; listed-but-missing-files renders the explicit state with the root named (I2/I3), no `StateError` leak.
- **AC2** — extension e2e: create the 2048 app in the extension, reopen panel, start — works; bundled `subscription-tracker` still works.
- **AC3** — divergence regression: a crafted OPFS state where the legacy list root sees an app the read root doesn't ⇒ list no longer shows it (or shows the missing-files state), covered by a REG test pinning root resolution.
- **AC4** — traversal ids (`../x`, absolute) are rejected at list and read.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — root-resolution helper: VM/web parity table; id validation.
- `IT-*` — MemoryExecutionEnv boot path (AC1); missing-manifest vs missing-js vs missing-dir each produce distinct honest messages.
- `E2E-*` — browser_ext e2e: install-then-open user app (AC2); restart persistence of stored apps.
- `REG-1` — CI: IT+UT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart`/web env; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — app deleted while its card is open → refresh to missing-files state, no crash. **E2** — invalid manifest.json → validation error naming the field (#1616 shares the validator). **E3** — OPFS quota errors → honest message, not "entry not found".

## Non-goals
- No app sync across devices; no bundling user apps into the extension build; no widget-permission changes (#1616's scope); no redesign of the Apps tab.

## Open questions
1. Should cross-host leftovers (listed but never persisted) be **hidden** or shown with the missing-files state? *Sketched default: hidden behind a "show broken apps" toggle — honest but quiet.*
2. Root fix in `_AppWidgetFileReader` vs introducing a shared `AppStorage` facade — implementer's call within I1.

## References
- #1614 (original: YuryBY, with file:line analysis), #1616 (unpacked-widget load path shares the validator), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, `browser_ext/panel/app/assets/apps/`.

Only `subscription-tracker` is bundled; user apps come from OPFS storage. Listing shows the app while reading fails → roots diverge. Reproduce, fix list/read divergence, make failure actionable, regression-test via MemoryExecutionEnv + extension e2e.

Decision: the minimal-risk, review-compliant move is to route the remaining sites through AppStorage NOW — it is small, mechanical, and eliminates the important finding entirely instead of leaving it to a fast-forward ticket. The concrete defect named: `removeWidget` fed a raw agent-supplied id — a traversal id (`../evil`) would `listDir('apps/../evil')` and `remove('apps/../evil/...')` — escaping the namespace on removal (delete outside apps/!). That IS a real boundary issue on the remove path (deletion, not just listing): an agent calling `widgets_catalog remove ../something` could delete files outside the namespace recursively. The review downplays it ("the agent already has env-wide file access") but the fix is cheap and testable.

   - `_seedDemoApp` — demo ids are code-controlled, no test needed beyond existing.

Decision: the minimal-risk, review-compliant move is to route the remaining sites through AppStorage NOW — it is small, mechanical, and eliminates the important finding entirely instead of leaving it to a fast-forward ticket. BUT the TDD rule requires a reproducing test first for any production change. The concrete defect named: `removeWidget` fed a raw agent-supplied id — a traversal id (`../evil`) would `listDir('apps/../evil')` and `remove('apps/../evil/...')` — escaping the namespace on removal (delete outside apps/!). That IS a real boundary issue on the remove path (deletion, not just listing): an agent calling `widgets_catalog remove ../something` could delete files outside the namespace recursively. The review downplays it ("the agent already has env-wide file access") but the fix is cheap and testable.

Plan (TDD):
1. RED: add tests in `test/apps_store_test.dart` (or the namespace IT):
   - `removeWidget` with a traversal id (`../evil`) throws ArgumentError and removes nothing (today: no throw — it would attempt `listDir('apps/../evil')` which in MemoryExecutionEnv... may return not-found Result and then proceed to remove nothing, or worse delete outside). Need to check what MemoryExecutionEnv does with `apps/../evil` — path normalization? Let me check the fake env used in tests.
   - `missingInstalledFiles` / `isEmptyAppDir` with hostile id → ArgumentError (or false-y safe).
   - `_seedDemoApp` — demo ids are code-controlled, no test needed beyond existing.

content.thinking:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).
- `availableUpdates`: entry.id hostile → manifestPath... use `isResolvableId` skip + log (a catalog id that cannot live in the namespace is never installable — installWidget's own validation rejects it; skipping the update probe is honest).
- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

These are all "route through the one resolver" changes — exactly the reviewer's important finding. No behavior regression for legit ids; hostile inputs fail closed without crashing healers.

1. `removeWidget throws ArgumentError for a traversal id and removes nothing` — drive `removeWidget('../evil')` (force: true AND force: false) → expect throws ArgumentError; assert env has no removal outside namespace (fake env records? simplest: the test env is MemoryExecutionEnv — create `apps/keep/widget.js` + a sibling top-level `evil/widget.js`... `apps/../evil` from the apps root — in MemoryExecutionEnv paths are env-relative; `apps/../evil` may normalize. Let me check MemoryExecutionEnv's path handling. If it normalizes `..`, then today removeWidget('../evil', force: true) would listDir('evil')... wait `apps/../evil` → `evil` — and remove `evil/<name>` recursively → DELETES OUTSIDE APPS. That's the demonstrable escape. Test: seed `secret/keep.txt` outside apps (env root), call removeWidget('../secret', force: true), expect throws + file still exists. Today (RED): no throw and secret deleted? Depends on MemoryExecutionEnv normalization — check.
2. `isEmptyAppDir returns false for a traversal id` (no throw).
3. `missingInstalledFiles ignores a tampered record naming paths outside the namespace` — write `.installed.json` with hostile rel `../../outside.txt` + create `outside.txt` at env root; expect result doesn't probe outside → hmm, what's the observable? `missing` should contain `../../outside.txt` (treated missing → healer reinstalls) or []. Decide: treat as missing (damage). Assert: returns ['../../outside.txt'] AND (key assertion) the outside file is untouched (no exists-escape observable... exists doesn't mutate; the escape is only an info-read — the honest assert is just the returned list + no crash).
4. `isCleanInstall returns false for a tampered record with a hostile id` — meta with id '../evil' + files; expect false, no crash.
5. `availableUpdates skips catalog ids that cannot live in the namespace` — catalog entry id '../evil' with newer version + installed meta... simpler: expect empty update list, no crash.

Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).

- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).
- `availableUpdates`: entry.id hostile → manifestPath... use `isResolvableId` skip + log (a catalog id that cannot live in the namespace is never installable — installWidget's own validation rejects it; skipping the update probe is honest).
- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

These are all "route through the one resolver" changes — exactly the reviewer's important finding. No behavior regression for legit ids; hostile inputs fail closed without crashing healers.

If it normalizes `..`, then today removeWidget('../evil', force: true) would listDir('evil')... wait `apps/../evil` → `evil` — and remove `evil/<name>` recursively → DELETES OUTSIDE APPS. That's the demonstrable escape. Test: seed `secret/keep.txt` outside apps (env root), call removeWidget('../secret', force: true), expect throws + file still exists. Today (RED): no throw and secret deleted? Depends on MemoryExecutionEnv normalization — check.
2. `isEmptyAppDir returns false for a traversal id` (no throw).
3. `missingInstalledFiles ignores a tampered record naming paths outside the namespace` — write `.installed.json` with hostile rel `../../outside.txt` + create `outside.txt` at env root; expect result doesn't probe outside → hmm, what's the observable? `missing` should contain `../../outside.txt` (treated missing → healer reinstalls) or []. Decide: treat as missing (damage). Assert: returns ['../../outside.txt'] AND (key assertion) the outside file is untouched (no exists-escape observable... exists doesn't mutate; the escape is only an info-read — the honest assert is just the returned list + no crash).

With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).
- `availableUpdates`: entry.id hostile → manifestPath... use `isResolvableId` skip + log (a catalog id that cannot live in the namespace is never installable — installWidget's own validation rejects it; skipping the update probe is honest).
- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

blocks.text:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).
- `availableUpdates`: entry.id hostile → manifestPath... use `isResolvableId` skip + log (a catalog id that cannot live in the namespace is never installable — installWidget's own validation rejects it; skipping the update probe is honest).
- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

blocks.text:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. blocks.text:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. blocks.text:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too. Gate: `if (entry == null) return false;` covers hostile ids without a record; a TAMPERED meta with hostile id + files map → walk('apps/../evil') escape-lists. Gate with `isResolvableId` → return false before walking.)
- `missingInstalledFiles(id)`: hostile id → meta lookup null → files null → return []. Tampered meta hostile id + files → escape exists-probes. Gate with isResolvableId → return const []. Per-rel: isValidRelativePath gate → count as missing (honest: healer reinstalls).
- `availableUpdates`: entry.id hostile → manifestPath... use `isResolvableId` skip + log (a catalog id that cannot live in the namespace is never installable — installWidget's own validation rejects it; skipping the update probe is honest).
- `_seedDemoApp`: `AppStorage.manifestPath(id)` / `AppStorage.appFile(id, file.key)` — code-controlled ids; throws only on a dev mistake (fail-closed good).
- `resetToFactory`/`listAppDirIds`: `AppStorage.root` for the listDir root constant (cosmetic consistency, no behavior change).

blocks.text:
The auto-update flows iterate `result.entries` (remote catalog) — untrusted ids. The healing loops wrap in try/catch, so a throw from the store would be logged, not crash. But `isCleanInstall`/`isEmptyAppDir`/`missingInstalledFiles` calls at the top of those iterations are INSIDE no try... actually `isCleanInstall(entry.id)` at line 32 is not in a try; `isEmptyAppDir` at 65 is not; `missingInstalledFiles(entry.id)` at 95 is not. A hostile catalog id throwing ArgumentError would crash `runCatalogAutoUpdate` — need to check its caller... it's probably awaited in the launcher with its own try/catch. Regardless: throwing on a hostile CATALOG id turns one bad catalog entry into "auto-update crashed" — worse than skipping. The store methods are fine to throw (fail-closed contract), but these auto-update call sites should skip non-resolvable ids. Hmm — that's growing scope.

Alternative minimal design that avoids touching catalog_auto_update at all: make the store methods THROWS-free for hostile ids by returning the safe negative:
- `removeWidget`: hostile id → ArgumentError? or `false`? Today: hostile id → `meta.containsKey('../x')` false → return false (nothing removed — the meta gate ALREADY protects the non-force path!). The dangerous path is `force: true`... force callers pass listed ids. Actually wait — reconsider the actual exploitability: without force, meta lookup fails → return false. With force, only UI paths (listed ids). The tool path (untrusted) uses force:false. So TODAY the raw-id ingress is already gated by the meta check — the review says "No privilege boundary crossed today". The interpolation issue is consistency/defense (I1 "no second path normalization"), plus `meta.containsKey` with a hostile key is harmless.

So the honest scope: make the store's path MATH go through AppStorage so "no second path normalization" is true, with failure modes that don't regress the auto-update healer:
- `removeWidget(appId)`: resolve `AppStorage.appDir(appId)` — but ONLY after the meta/force gate? No — compute dir first; hostile id → ArgumentError. Tool path: hostile id → ArgumentError propagates out of removeWidget → _mutate has no catch → tool result error. Actually how do tools handle exceptions? Probably the tool runner catches and returns error text. That's an honest error for a hostile input. But better UX + reviewer's exact ask: gate at the tool with tryAppDir first ("validate the widgets_catalog remove id with tryAppDir") and keep store throwing.
- `isEmptyAppDir(id)`: called with catalog ids (untrusted). Hostile → today listDir('apps/../x') → in most envs resolves to a real dir outside → non-empty → false → skip healing. Fine already. With appDir throw → crashes healer loop. To keep healer robust I'd add resolvable-gate in store: `if (!AppStorage.isResolvableId(id)) return false;` — a hostile "app dir" is never an empty app dir; false = "nothing to heal" = skip. Honest and safe.
- `isCleanInstall(id)`: hostile → meta lookup fails first (`meta[id]` null → return false). Already safe. Route walk/read paths through AppStorage anyway (record exists only for real installs; id must be resolvable to have a record... actually meta keys could be tampered too.
